candidates.name: Neurolymphomatosis
support_spans: Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement
Enhancement of several cranial nerves including bilateral vagus nerves
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging studies suggest involvement of the nervous system by a lymphomatous process.

candidates.name: Lymphomatous Meningitis
support_spans: Lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features on light microscopy
κ light chain–restricted B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation
candidates.why: The cerebrospinal fluid analysis reveals lymphocytosis with plasmacytoid features, indicating a lymphomatous process involving the meninges.

candidates.name: Vagus Nerve Lymphoma
support_spans: Enhancement of several cranial nerves including bilateral vagus nerves
candidates.why: The imaging studies show enhancement of the vagus nerves, suggesting involvement by a lymphomatous process.

candidates.name: Intracranial Lymphoma
support_spans: Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement
Intraparenchymal ventral medullary enhancement
candidates.why: The imaging studies reveal diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement and intraparenchymal ventral medullary enhancement, indicating an intracranial lymphomatous process.

candidates.name: Secondary Central Nervous System Lymphoma
support_spans: The patient received chemotherapy (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, vincristine, and prednisone) followed by autologous peripheral blood stem cell transplant
candidates.why: The patient's history of chemotherapy and stem cell transplant increases the risk of secondary central nervous system lymphoma.
